quick.summary: Why warnings fail, and how to stop users from making huge mistakes.
quick.takeaway: Do not just warn the user. Put a physical hurdle in their way.

beats.line: Users keep deleting teams by mistake. Why does the warning pop up fail?
Think of a kitchen blender. A warning label does not stop the mess.
So the maker adds a lock. It will not spin without the lid.
You physically cannot do the wrong thing.
Exactly. To stop big mistakes, we add a forcing function.
Can I just say make it hard?
Yes. Put a small hurdle in the way.
Make them type the team name, not just click a button.
So I slow them down on purpose to save them from disaster.
And they will thank you for it.

quiz.question: How do you best stop users from deleting their account by accident?
options: Make them type their account name to confirm.
Make the delete button bright red.
Add a pop up that asks if they are sure.
Send them an email warning them first.
quiz.explanation: Typing a name is a forcing function. It makes the dangerous action physically harder to do.

quiz.question: A forcing function works by slowing the user down on purpose.
quiz.explanation: True. It introduces a little bit of friction to ensure the user is paying attention before taking a destructive action.
